newsitem.title: USA: Rain due in US Plains, western Midwest - forecaster.
newsitem.headline: Rain due in US Plains, western Midwest - forecaster.

text.p: Rain was forecast for much of the U.S. Great Plains and western Midwest Friday through Sunday morning with up to 2.0 inches from North Dakota to Oklahoma, and up to 1.5 inches in Minnesota, Missouri and Iowa, said Fred Gesser, Weather Express Inc meteorologist.
Lesser rain amounts were likely in the eastern Midwest during the weekend, but another storm system may produce up to 1.5 inches in that area Monday or Tuesday, he said.
"One (weather) model suggests the lightest rain will occur in central Illinois," Gesser said of next week's storms.
Gesser said the models suggest much of next week's storms will track north of central Illinois, which has been largely missed by summer rain.
Forecasters said an area bordered by the Illinois cities of Springfield, Decatur and Peoria, has largely been missed by summer storms.
National Weather Service data shows Peoria has received 0.53 inch of rain the past 30 days or 13 percent of normal.

In the Great Plains, the rain should be replaced early next week by hot, dry weather, which should allow the wheat harvest to resume. High temperatures from Kansas to Texas then should range from the 90s to 100 degrees Fahrenheit, with the 100 degree readings mostly in Texas.

Midwest temperatures should peak in the high 80s to low 90s through the weekend, but dip to the high 70s to low 80s early in the week. However, by July 18 highs should return to the high 80s to mid-90s in the western Midwest, he said.
